1 شَمَخَ , (S, L, K,) aor.
شَمُخَ , inf. n. شُمُوخٌ, (L,) It (a mountain) was high, or lofty. (S, L, K.) ―
-b2- Hence, (Har p. 442,) شَمَخَ بِأَنْفِهِ, (S, A, L, K,) and شَمَخَ أَنْفُهُ, aor. and inf. n. as above, (L,) He (a man) magnified, or exalted, himself; was proud; (S, A, L, K;) behaved proudly, or disdainfully; elevated his nose, from pride. (L.) [See also زَمَخَ.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
